That's for `getServerState` for the pages router, as with dynamic widgets we *mount* the provided component a second time, we don't receive a response from recommend anymore as the results were cached.
Maybe the problem is that in the helper when there are no queries to be made it doesn't raise any event : https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/e55c345bce1969f4379db39de27642a7929c9411/packages/algoliasearch-helper/src/algoliasearch.helper.js#L1636-L1638

body: It is, otherwise we would have `recommendResults` in `useSearchResults` which we haven't decided yet. Problem is `getIndexSearchResults` is both used by this and `getServerState`
It's in the `initialResults` passed from the first render
No, as it will resolve when search has been received and `_hasRecommendWidget = false`, although I guess we would have a hanging listener
ok sounds fair, maybe a comment to explain that this is to prevent recommend results? not sure if needed though
What do you mean by broken response ? I made one with an undefined `recommendResults` which could happen if they don't have recommend widgets

Good point, and I did do a benchmark : https://jsbench.me/oulwm3j29m/1
It's not as big a difference I thought would be on Chromium surprisingly (it is on WebKit though I guess ?), but still it's better yeah :D

I would have preferred it that way, unfortunately `_hasSearchWidget` and `_hasRecommendWidget` will always be `false` at this point as we initialize the promise before adding any widget.
This is one of the use cases where an event-based API makes sense. I could do that in the "legacy" `waitForResults` though, but maybe it's best to keep consistency.

All I could find was this : https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/e55c345bce1969f4379db39de27642a7929c9411/packages/vue-instantsearch/src/util/createServerRootMixin.js#L183-L196
We only validate if `initialResults` is truthy, we don't check any of its properties.
Anyway Vue doesn't have recommend widgets so `state` and `results` would still be defined.
We don't allow `Object.assign` in babel config 🙃 (`merge` is in the helper too)
Ah, I thought about it but was sure in my mind they would be set. Nevermind then!

can go back to spread then (but maybe leave a comment about `const recommendCache = Object.assign({}, ...Object.keys(initialResults).map(key => initialResults[key].recommendResults.results))` as the next major option, seems like that's quicker still (difference much bigger in safari than in chrome though) https://jsbench.me/9zlworivz7/1
